The durable mechanism is switching costs in professional creative workflows plus recurring revenue; the counter-assumption is that generative AI compresses its pricing, which is precisely why this is a contrarian, high-risk holding rather than a defensive one. At 5% it adds a second duration-sensitive franchise without doubling the software risk.
positions.catalyst: Evidence that generative features drive net new subscriptions and seat expansion rather than price erosion.
positions.invalidation: Sustained deceleration in net new recurring revenue or widespread downgrades of creative subscriptions.

positions.name: iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF
positions.thesis: This ETF holds long-dated US Treasuries, and the world claim that restrictive real rates eventually force an easing cycle applies at 81.96, near the 52-week low of 77.11 and about 7% below the 52-week high of 88.09 after a -4.8% twelve-month return, so the market is pricing almost no chance of a policy turn. The mechanism is simple duration: if growth slows and yields fall, long bonds re-rate; if inflation re-accelerates, this position loses and the thesis is wrong. At 3% it is a deliberately small convex hedge that should appreciate in the scenario where the equity sleeves are under stress from growth, not from inflation.
positions.catalyst: Softening labour or inflation data that brings forward expected policy easing.
positions.invalidation: A re-acceleration in inflation or fiscal supply that drives long yields to new highs.

At 8% it is the larger half of the crypto barbell because it is the most liquid and least protocol-specific expression of the thesis, sized so a 60% loss costs the book about five points.

positions.invalidation: A second consecutive year in which Bitcoin fails to protect against monetary expansion while real rates rise, or a regulatory or custody breakdown that impairs access.

positions.name: Ethereum spot pair

The assumptions I am making are that network usage and the monetary premium persist and that the asset does not lose share permanently to alternative chains; note that one small token in the packet (NEAR-USD.CC) rose 166% over twelve months, so I cannot claim the whole complex is cheap. At 4% it is half the Bitcoin weight because it carries both monetary and protocol risk.
positions.catalyst: Falling real yields plus a recovery in on-chain activity and fee burn relative to issuance.
positions.invalidation: Sustained loss of activity and fee share to other chains, or a supply or staking-mechanics change that erodes the monetary premium.

pick.knowledgeLimitations: I cannot verify any current valuation multiple, earnings figure, backlog, capital-expenditure guidance, oil price, policy rate or inflation reading, because the packet supplies only price, three- and twelve-month returns and 52-week ranges. I therefore infer macro conditions only from price action across ETFs, which is a noisy signal. I also cannot tell whether some price levels reflect share splits or other corporate actions, since several symbols sit far from the levels in my memory (for example NFLX.US at 63.95, MU.US at 733.15, SMCI.US at 28.60 and AMZN.US at 266.93), so I treat the snapshot prices as the only price truth and I avoided names whose decline I could not explain. I do not know why ORCL.US, INTU.US, ADBE.US or the semiconductor names fell, and my reasons about why they are cheap are assumptions about business durability, not verified facts. Crypto history in the packet omits weekend extremes, and no follow-up data or trading is allowed after sealing.

strategies.riskRationale: This book concentrates roughly half of capital in seven contrarian AI-compute and semiconductor-equipment holdings that are already 25-50% below their 52-week highs, plus a power-scarcity sleeve, deeply oversold long-duration software, a small long-Treasury option and a 12% crypto barbell, with only 3% cash. That profile is consistent with the high-risk objective because the expected upside comes from uncertain and contrarian reversals rather than defensive diversification, and because the same macro reversal (easing real rates and stabilised AI capital spending) drives most of the book, I accept an estimated maximum peak-to-trough drawdown of about 0.35 during the twelve months, with a plausible adverse case of 45-50% if the AI capex cycle contracts. A twelve-month horizon is long enough for one or two reporting cycles to confirm or break the capex thesis but short enough that the book is deliberately not built for long-run compounding; it is built for a specific re-rating window.

pick.risks: The main risks are that defensives have already re-rated sharply and could de-rate with the market (XLP is only about 1% below its 52-week high, JNJ sits exactly at its 52-week high after a 54% twelve-month gain), that a growth re-acceleration or a sharp bond rally would leave this book well behind SPY because of its 35% cash-and-bonds drag, that a hard recession would still produce a 10% to 15% equity drawdown despite defensive sectors, that gold and equities can fall together in a liquidity squeeze, and that the defensive sleeve is factor-correlated even though the sector revenue drivers differ, so the true diversification is lower than the count of holdings suggests.

theses.title: Real rates stay restrictive
theses.worldView: Central banks will keep inflation-adjusted policy rates above zero through the target horizon, because inflation settles somewhat above the pre-2021 comfort zone and large government deficits keep the term premium elevated, so cash-flow-distant and long-duration assets stay priced off a high discount rate instead of returning to zero-rate conditions.
theses.portfolioExpression: The book keeps equity risk in short-duration, cash-generative franchises, keeps fixed income in short and intermediate Treasuries and core bonds that earn carry at today's yields, holds 15% cash as optionality, and owns no long-duration speculative growth and no crypto, which I would regard as the wrong asset class for a restrictive-rate, low-risk mandate.

theses.title: Nominal growth cools from a cyclical peak
theses.worldView: The very large twelve-month rebounds visible in the snapshot for oil, refiners, memory chips and some financials will decelerate into slower nominal GDP and slower earnings growth over the next two years without a deep recession, so revenue visibility and pricing power matter more than cyclical torque.
theses.portfolioExpression: The portfolio overweights staples, regulated utilities, healthcare, wireless telecom and other contracted-revenue businesses whose demand is inelastic, and deliberately avoids the cyclicals whose twelve-month returns of 80% to 100% plus already price in a strong rebound.

theses.title: Fiscal and geopolitical risk keeps a hedge bid
theses.worldView: Sustained government debt loads, fragmented trade and recurring geopolitical or policy-error shocks mean at least one risk-off episode occurs within 24 months, and that gold retains a reserve-asset role alongside the dollar rather than being permanently demonetized.
theses.portfolioExpression: A 5% GLD position sized as insurance rather than as a return engine, together with 15% cash, expresses the view that the portfolio must survive a shock without selling equities at the bottom.

theses.title: Capital rotates from crowded growth to balance-sheet quality
theses.worldView: Expensive, crowded long-duration equity themes continue to de-rate while discount rates stay high, whereas profitable, low-leverage businesses with durable free cash flow hold or gain relative value, so a diversified value tilt beats the growth complex over a two-year view.
theses.portfolioExpression: VTV, BRK-B, Walmart and the defensive equity sleeve apply this rotation through diversified, cash-returning balance sheets, instead of making single-stock bets on the beaten-up technology names in the packet that are already down 30% to 50% from their highs.

pick.thesis: A softer nominal-growth world with still-positive real rates argues for buying contracted cash flows, short-duration carry and hedges rather than cyclical torque or long-duration growth, so the book is roughly 60% defensive and value equity, 20% short and intermediate bonds, 5% gold and 15% cash, built to compound modestly and to survive a drawdown without selling anything for two years.

forecasts.reason: A total return near +10% over 24 months requires a soft-landing world in which inflation drifts toward the 2% to 3% range, policy rates stay positive in real terms but ease gradually, and nominal growth slows without a deep recession, so that roughly 60% defensive equity compounds about 6% to 7% a year from dividends and modest value re-rating, the 20% bond sleeve earns around 4% to 5% a year from carry with some duration help, gold adds little or modestly, and the 15% cash drag earns nothing; this is plausible rather than certain, a recession would cut the outcome toward low single digits or negative, and a growth melt-up would leave this book well behind the broad market.

positions.name: iShares 1-3 Year Treasury Bond ETF
positions.thesis: SHY holds short-maturity US Treasuries, so in a world where policy rates stay positive in real terms the fund collects the short rate with very little price volatility, which is exactly the low-duration stance a restrictive-rate view demands; the packet shows 81.59 with a roughly +1.8% twelve-month adjusted return, consistent with earning carry and minimal duration loss, and I assume yields remain positive in real terms although I cannot verify their level. This is the portfolio's lowest-volatility return engine, and at 12% it is sized so that even a large rate move changes the position value only slightly.
positions.catalyst: Sustained disinflation that lets the central bank ease into a soft landing would add duration gains to the carry, and any equity drawdown would raise demand for short Treasuries.
positions.invalidation: A renewed inflation surge would erode the real return of this sleeve and a rapid return to near-zero rates would make its yield uncompetitive with equities, either of which would break the restrictive-rate application at this weight.

positions.name: iShares Core U.S. Aggregate Bond ETF
positions.thesis: AGG is a diversified investment-grade index of Treasuries, agencies, corporates and mortgage-backed bonds trading at 96.58 with an essentially flat twelve-month price return, which I read as yields having risen enough to offset modest duration losses and to provide an income anchor that equities cannot supply in a slower-growth world. I assume its credit quality and duration remain broadly index-like, which the packet cannot confirm, and I keep it at 8% so the book has genuine ballast without becoming a bond bet.
positions.catalyst: Inflation drifting back toward target and a gradual easing cycle would lift this holding through both carry and duration appreciation.
positions.invalidation: A re-acceleration of inflation or a fiscal term-premium shock pushing yields sharply higher would extend the flat-to-down price pattern and invalidate the case for holding intermediate duration here.

positions.name: Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR
positions.thesis: XLP holds food, beverage, household and personal-care companies whose demand is inelastic, so if nominal growth cools from the cyclical highs implied by the snapshot's energy and memory returns, staples volumes, margins and dividends hold up while cyclical earnings fall, and pricing power converts cost inflation into revenue. I acknowledge the sector has already re-rated, with the fund at 90.89 against a 52-week high of 91.94 and a +23.5% twelve-month return, so this is bought for drawdown control rather than for cheapness, and the 10% core weight reflects that it is a defensive anchor rather than a valuation conviction.
positions.catalyst: Steady dividend growth and volume recovery as input-cost inflation fades, plus defensive inflows whenever growth data weaken.
positions.invalidation: A hard recession compressing staples volumes and margins, or a broad valuation de-rating that drags this sector down with the market, would show that defensiveness alone was not a value anchor.

positions.name: Utilities Select Sector SPDR
positions.thesis: XLU holds regulated electric and gas utilities whose allowed returns are set by regulators and whose demand is supported by electrification and data-center power needs, so in a slower-nominal-growth world regulated rate-base growth plus dividends is a comparatively durable return stream with less industrial cyclicality. The packet shows 43.79 with only a +1.8% twelve-month return against a 52-week high of 46.75, meaning this sector has participated far less in the defensive re-rating than staples or healthcare, and at 8% I accept its interest-rate sensitivity in exchange for that steadier cash-flow mechanism.
positions.catalyst: Lower financing costs from an easing cycle let allowed returns convert into stronger dividend growth, while long-term power contracts raise regulated investment.
positions.invalidation: A renewed rise in long-term yields pressuring the sector's dividend-spread valuation, or regulators denying rate-base growth, would break the cash-flow mechanism this position relies on.

positions.name: Health Care Select Sector SPDR
positions.thesis: XLV gives diversified exposure to pharmaceuticals, managed care, medical devices and life-science tools whose demand is driven by demographics and health need rather than by the business cycle, which is what a growth-downshift world rewards; the sector's +31.2% twelve-month return to 188.33 reflects renewed confidence in drug pricing and pipelines rather than a cyclical boom. Using an ETF rather than single names keeps drug-trial and litigation risk diffuse, and 8% is a size that adds recession-resistant earnings without letting healthcare policy risk dominate the book.
positions.catalyst: Continued volume growth in major drug franchises and clearer, less punitive drug-pricing policy.
positions.invalidation: Aggressive US drug-price controls, another managed-care margin shock, or a broad de-rating of healthcare multiples would invalidate the defensive application at this price.

positions.name: Berkshire Hathaway Class B
positions.thesis: BRK-B is a diversified conglomerate spanning insurance, railroads, energy, industrial and consumer businesses plus a large liquidity reserve, so in a world where discount rates stay high and crowded growth themes de-rate, an unlevered balance sheet, insurance float and retained free cash flow compound without needing multiple expansion; its own cash also lets it buy assets during a dislocation, which links it to the hedge thesis. The packet shows 575.25, close to the 52-week high of 579.09 after a +16.6% twelve-month return, so this is quality at a fair price rather than a deep-value trade, and 12% is the largest weight because the earnings base is already diversified across sectors.
positions.catalyst: Capital deployment at attractive prices, profitable insurance underwriting, and repurchases when the shares trade below intrinsic value.
positions.invalidation: A severe recession hitting railroad and industrial earnings, a hard turn in insurance markets, a large poor-price acquisition, or an erosion of capital-allocation discipline after succession would show this weight was not defensive enough.

positions.name: Johnson & Johnson
positions.thesis: JNJ is a diversified healthcare company with pharmaceutical and medical-technology franchises and a long record of dividend growth, so in a slower-nominal-growth world its inelastic demand, pricing power and financial strength make its cash flows a defensive anchor; the packet shows the shares at 282.11, exactly their 52-week high after a +54.3% twelve-month return, which is a valuation risk I accept only at 5% for the durability of the earnings stream. The price and return facts come from the packet, while the assumption that the dividend remains well covered is mine and cannot be verified from the data supplied.
positions.catalyst: Continued growth in oncology and immunology drugs, medical-technology volume recovery, and steady dividend increases.
positions.invalidation: A major litigation charge, a patent-cliff revenue loss larger than the pipeline replaces, or a de-rating from the 52-week high would show that the price already fully discounted the defensiveness.

positions.name: Walmart Inc.
positions.thesis: Walmart is a grocery-led retailer whose scale and price position let it gain share and protect margins when consumers trade down during a slower nominal-growth period, which is precisely the world this book expects; the packet shows 125.66 with a +24.6% twelve-month return and +11.2% over three months, so the market already recognizes the share-gain story and I buy it for earnings resilience and dividend growth rather than for a demonstrably cheap multiple. At 5% it contributes consumer-staples-like cash flows with more operating leverage than XLP, which is why it is half the size of the staples ETF.
positions.catalyst: Share gains from higher-income households, growth in advertising and marketplace revenue, and continued operating-margin improvement.
positions.invalidation: Consumer weakness that pressures margins, e-commerce competition that halts share gains, or wage inflation that compresses profitability would invalidate the resilience thesis at this price.

positions.name: Verizon Communications
positions.thesis: Verizon is a wireless carrier with contracted subscription revenue and high switching costs, so in a restrictive-rate, slower-growth world its cash flows are defensive and its income stream is more attractive than the flat cash yield the benchmark pays; the packet shows 46.06 within a 52-week range of 37.12 to 50.66 after a +23.4% twelve-month return, a modest-priced holding compared with defensives sitting at their highs. I assume the dividend remains covered by free cash flow and that leverage drifts lower, assumptions the packet cannot verify, and I cap it at 4% because a capital-intensive leveraged telecom carries more single-name and balance-sheet risk than the ETF sleeves.
positions.catalyst: Fixed-wireless subscriber growth, continued debt reduction, and dividend growth backed by free cash flow.
positions.invalidation: A wireless price war compressing margins, a dividend cut or rising leverage, or sustained capital-expenditure overruns would break the income-and-stability application.

positions.name: Vanguard Value ETF
positions.thesis: VTV holds a diversified basket of large and mid-capitalization US value companies across financials, healthcare, industrials, energy and staples at lower earnings multiples than the growth complex, so with the discount rate staying high and crowded long-duration themes in the packet already down 30% to 50% from their highs, buying the cheaper cash-returning half of the market is the diversified way to apply the rotation without stock-picking risk. The fund is at 227.38 after a +25.4% twelve-month return, meaning the rotation has already started and I am not calling a bottom, and 8% gives real value exposure while the ETF structure keeps single-name risk diffuse.
positions.catalyst: Value-sector earnings outperformance as growth multiples compress, and a broadening of market leadership beyond a handful of very large technology names.
positions.invalidation: A fresh AI-led growth acceleration that lifts long-duration multiples sharply, or a deep recession that hits the financials and cyclicals inside the index, would leave this tilt lagging and break the rotation thesis.

positions.name: SPDR Gold Shares
positions.thesis: GLD holds gold bullion and therefore gives the book a monetary and crisis hedge that does not depend on corporate earnings, which suits a world of large fiscal deficits, fragmented trade and periodic policy error in which gold retains a reserve-asset role; the packet shows 379.53 against a 52-week high of 495.90 and low of 355.78, roughly 23% below its high, so I am entering after a drawdown rather than at the peak, though I cannot verify why gold fell or what real rates are today. The 5% weight is insurance sized to cushion a risk-off episode without turning the portfolio into a commodity bet.
positions.catalyst: Renewed central-bank gold buying, a geopolitical or credit shock, or a genuine easing cycle that lowers real yields.
positions.invalidation: A sustained rise in real yields and a strong dollar pushing gold below its 52-week low, or evidence that reserve managers are structurally selling gold, would show the hedge role is broken and leave this 5% as dead weight.

pick.knowledgeLimitations: The packet supplies only adjusted prices, three- and twelve-month returns and 52-week ranges, so I cannot verify current valuations, earnings, dividend coverage, balance sheets, interest-rate levels, index multiples or any news after the cutoff; my reading that bond yields offer real carry is inferred from price levels such as AGG at 96.58 and SHY at 81.59 plus long-run relationships, not from verified rate data. I also cannot verify why gold sits about 23% below its 52-week high, whether defensive multiples are reasonable, whether Verizon's dividend and leverage remain sound, or that no company-specific shock hits JNJ, Walmart or Berkshire, and I assume the packet's adjusted closes embed dividends.

strategies.riskRationale: This is a two-year capital-preservation book: about 60% diversified defensive and value equity, 20% short and intermediate investment-grade fixed income, 5% gold as insurance, and 15% cash that is an explicit thesis position rather than a leftover, because the packet gives me no valuations or rate levels to verify and because dry powder lets a drawdown be an opportunity instead of a forced sale. The deliberately defensive 40% non-equity share caps realistic upside near 10% over 24 months in exchange for a materially smaller peak-to-trough decline than a broad equity index, which fits a low-risk objective better than chasing the snapshot's already-completed cyclical rebounds.

pick.risks: Main risks are a demand-led energy and commodity price collapse that would hurt T2 holdings simultaneously, a hard credit recession that would hit banks and managed care together, an actual AI capex bust rather than digestion that would punish NVDA, GOOGL, MSFT and AMZN at once, and correlation risk among US large caps, since most holdings share sensitivity to nominal growth and to liquidity shocks. Concentration is moderate: the largest holding is 8% (BRK-B.US), the top five total 27%, and the only deliberately speculative sleeve is 3.5% in crypto, but a broad US equity drawdown of 25-30% would drag most of the book regardless of individual quality, which is why I estimate a 22% maximum drawdown rather than a low-risk number. Because the portfolio is never rebalanced, weights will drift and any position that doubles becomes a larger concentration, a risk I accept deliberately.

theses.title: AI capex digestion, not an AI bust
theses.worldView: Over the next 24 months global spending on compute, networking, data-center power and the software that monetizes it keeps compounding at high single-digit to double-digit rates even though the market has already cut AI-hardware and software prices sharply from their 2026 highs, so cash-generative franchises along the AI value chain are de-risked rather than broken at current prices.
theses.portfolioExpression: About 21% of capital sits in diversified AI value-chain cash-flow leaders (NVDA.US, GOOGL.US, MSFT.US, AMZN.US) plus payment rails (V.US), sized so that a continued de-rating of any single name cannot dominate the book.

theses.title: Fiscal-heavy reindustrialization, defense and power demand
theses.worldView: Large structural fiscal deficits, reshored industrial capacity, grid and data-center electrification and elevated defense procurement keep commodity and capital-goods demand firm through 2028, so energy producers, copper and machinery earn mid-cycle or better cash flows instead of sliding into a demand recession.
theses.portfolioExpression: About 24% of capital is in energy majors and E&P, copper, machinery, aerospace and defense, with Berkshire's rail, energy and manufacturing units adding the same exposure inside one balance sheet.

theses.title: Inflation settles sticky and real rates stay positive
theses.worldView: Inflation settles in roughly a 2.5-4% band with real policy rates still positive, rewarding businesses with pricing power, insurance float and short-duration cash flows and penalizing long-duration cash-burning growth, so value concentrates in cash compounders and financials rather than duration.
theses.portfolioExpression: About 29% of capital is in banks, managed care, pharmacy, pharma, staples and payment networks, plus Berkshire's float-backed structure, all of which earn on higher nominal rates and can raise price.

theses.title: Fiscal dominance keeps a bid under scarce hard and digital assets
theses.worldView: Sustained fiscal dominance and rising public debt keep a partial bid under scarce assets such as gold and bitcoin as hedges against currency debasement, even though these assets can fall 50% or more in real terms during rate-shock or liquidity-driven selloffs.
theses.portfolioExpression: A 7.5% combined position in GLD.US, BTC-USD.CC and ETH-USD.CC is capped small so that a 50% drawdown of the hedge sleeve costs less than 4% of total portfolio capital.

pick.thesis: The world view is that 2026-2028 is a mid-cycle, high-fiscal-deficit, sticky-inflation economy rather than either a 2021 melt-up or a 2008-style bust: AI and electrification capex continues while multiples de-rate, energy and industrial demand stays firm, and pricing-power compounders with float and cash flow outperform long-duration growth; the portfolio expresses this with a barbell of de-rated quality tech, hard-asset and industrial cyclicals, financials and defensive cash generators, plus a small hard-asset hedge and 10% cash. The internal tension is that the AI thesis (T1) wants rate-sensitive growth while the sticky-inflation thesis (T3) favors short duration; I resolve it by holding only profitable, cash-generative AI names at a combined 21% versus 29% in pricing-power and financial exposures, so the book is not a single-factor bet on rates.

forecasts.reason: A roughly +22% total return over 24 months is plausible if AI and electrification capital spending continues while multiples have already de-rated, energy and financial cash flows hold up under sticky inflation and positive real rates, and no hard credit recession occurs; that world implies mid-to-high single-digit annualized earnings growth plus modest multiple stability for a diversified book, with roughly 10% cash acting as drag and the small crypto and gold sleeves adding or subtracting a few points. The estimate is genuinely uncertain — a plausible band is roughly -15% to +45%, and it would prove too optimistic if a demand-led commodity collapse, an AI capex bust, or a credit recession arrived instead of the mid-cycle scenario I am assuming.

positions.name: Berkshire Hathaway Class B
positions.thesis: Berkshire is a float-backed conglomerate spanning insurance, railroads, energy, manufacturing and a large short-term securities pile, so in a world of sticky inflation and positive real rates its insurance float and cash earn more while its industrial and energy units ride reindustrialization, and at 575.25 against a 579.09 high (+16.6% over twelve months) the price buys resilience and deployment capacity rather than a cheap multiple; the evidence I rely on is the historical durability of float-funded compounding and opportunistic cash deployment, which is a known mechanism rather than a verified current balance sheet, and the 8% weight reflects its role as the book's anchor at medium risk.
positions.catalyst: Deployment of the cash pile into acquisitions or buybacks during a market dislocation, or an acceleration in insurance underwriting profit and investment income while nominal rates stay positive.
positions.invalidation: A deflationary rate collapse that destroys investment income combined with a major insurance, railroad or energy loss event would invalidate both the world thesis and this application, as would permanent capital impairment from overpaying for deals.

positions.name: Exxon Mobil
positions.thesis: Exxon Mobil is an integrated oil and gas producer expressing T2, because a world of firm energy demand from industrial policy, electrification and data-center power keeps integrated producers generating strong free cash flow for buybacks and dividends, and the packet already reflects that expectation with +48.0% over twelve months to 164.73 versus a 187.25 high, so I am assuming mid-cycle or better realizations and continued capital discipline rather than an energy price boom; the 5% weight makes it the largest single energy exposure without letting a crude collapse dominate the portfolio.
positions.catalyst: Sustained global oil, gas and LNG demand and project ramp-ups translating into continued buyback and dividend growth.
positions.invalidation: A demand-led collapse in crude and gas prices or a policy or regulatory shock that impairs project returns would invalidate this application of T2.

positions.name: Chevron
positions.thesis: Chevron is the second integrated major in the book so that T2 is applied to a diversified energy complex rather than to one operator, and in a world of firm energy demand its integrated cash flows and shareholder distributions support returns, with the packet showing 210.78 against a 235.52 high (+43.2% over twelve months); I assume continued capital discipline and treat the 3% weight as diversification within the energy thesis rather than a top-up of a single bet.
positions.catalyst: M&A or project execution that lifts free cash flow per share, or a firming of global demand that supports distributions.
positions.invalidation: Sustained weakness in commodity realizations or a major project or integration failure would break this application of the energy thesis.

positions.name: ConocoPhillips
positions.thesis: ConocoPhillips is a pure-play exploration and production company applying T2 at a discount to its own high, at 134.47 versus 154.03 after +61.9% over twelve months, because a world of firm demand and disciplined non-OPEC supply keeps shale and global E&P free cash flow strong enough for distributions; I assume shale productivity and shareholder-return discipline persist and size it at 2.5% because a pure E&P carries more commodity beta than an integrated major.
positions.catalyst: Buyback acceleration or a sustained firming of global crude demand and prices.
positions.invalidation: A supply glut or demand recession that pushes realizations below the cost of capital would invalidate the E&P expression of T2.

positions.name: Freeport-McMoRan
positions.thesis: Freeport-McMoRan is a copper producer expressing T2 through electrification, grid build-out and data-center power demand, where a world of reindustrialization and constrained new copper supply supports producer cash flows, and at 62.33 versus a 79.74 high with -9.3% over three months the market has already pulled it back from its 2026 peak despite +62.8% over twelve months; the evidence is the physical demand mechanism from electrification, which is an assumption about future adoption rather than a verified current order book, and 2.5% reflects copper's higher commodity beta.
positions.catalyst: Grid and data-center electrification projects accelerating copper demand, or supply constraints at major mines.
positions.invalidation: A China-driven industrial demand collapse, rapid copper substitution, or a wave of new mine supply would invalidate this application.

positions.name: Caterpillar
positions.thesis: Caterpillar is a machinery maker applying T2, because a world of reindustrialization, mining investment and infrastructure spending supports capital-goods orders and aftermarket margins, and the packet shows the stock at 598.88 versus a 1060.41 high after -28.8% over three months, a substantial de-rating I treat as a price fact rather than a verified signal about fundamentals; I assume mid-cycle machinery demand persists and size it at 3% because cyclical order books can fall quickly in a capex recession.
positions.catalyst: A recovery in machinery orders and backlog, or infrastructure and mining capex announcements.
positions.invalidation: A global capital-goods recession with falling orders and rising dealer inventories would invalidate this application of T2.

positions.name: Deere & Company
positions.thesis: Deere is an agricultural and construction equipment maker expressing T2 at 691.28 near its 707.79 high (+47.1% over twelve months), because a world of firm food demand, mechanization and infrastructure investment supports equipment volumes and precision-agriculture attach rates; I assume farm income stabilizes rather than collapses, and the 2.5% weight recognizes that agriculture is a distinct cycle from construction and mining.
positions.catalyst: A recovery in farm income and equipment replacement demand, or growth in precision-agriculture software revenue.
positions.invalidation: A prolonged compression in crop prices and farm income that defers equipment purchases would invalidate this application.

positions.name: GE Aerospace
positions.thesis: GE Aerospace is an aviation and industrial supplier applying T2, because a world of sustained air travel growth, elevated defense procurement and long-lived engine aftermarket revenue supports durable cash generation, and at 335.54 versus a 380.64 high it is priced below its own peak while the twelve-month return is +10.5%; I assume aftermarket demand and defense budgets persist and the 3% weight reflects quality industrial exposure with less commodity beta than energy.
positions.catalyst: Commercial engine deliveries and aftermarket shop visits accelerating, or large defense contract awards.
positions.invalidation: A travel downturn, supply-chain failure or a defense budget contraction would invalidate this application.

positions.name: Lockheed Martin
positions.thesis: Lockheed Martin is a defense prime expressing the fiscal side of T2 and the geopolitical strain behind T4, because a world of elevated geopolitical tension and structural fiscal deficits supports multi-year procurement of missiles, aircraft and space systems, and at 588.19 versus a 668.17 high the price is well below its peak despite +28.7% over twelve months; I assume defense budgets remain elevated in real terms, which is an assumption about policy rather than a verified appropriation, and the 2.5% weight keeps government-contract execution risk contained.
positions.catalyst: Multi-year missile and aircraft contract awards or an increase in allied European and Asian defense spending.
positions.invalidation: A peace dividend scenario with real defense budget cuts or major program cost overruns would invalidate this application.

positions.name: JPMorgan Chase
positions.thesis: JPMorgan is the largest US bank and expresses T3, because a world of positive real rates and sticky nominal growth supports net interest income, fee generation and credit normalization while its scale deposit franchise is a pricing-power asset, and at 342.08 versus a 363.37 high (-5.0% over three months) it is not priced at its peak despite +11.2% over twelve months; I assume a soft-landing credit cycle rather than a 2008-style loss wave, and 5% reflects both the durability of the franchise and the reality that bank equity is levered to credit.
positions.catalyst: Continued net interest income resilience, capital return increases, or a capital-markets deal recovery.
positions.invalidation: A hard credit recession with rising charge-offs and loan-loss provisions would invalidate both the bank application and the soft-landing part of the world thesis.

positions.name: Bank of America
positions.thesis: Bank of America applies T3 as a consumer and commercial deposit franchise that earns more when nominal rates stay positive, and at 50.55 versus a 64.48 high after -20.6% over three months it is one of the more de-rated large banks in the packet, which I treat as a price fact and not as verified bad news; I assume deposit costs stabilize and credit stays benign, and the 3% weight keeps single-bank credit risk smaller than the sector's total allocation.
positions.catalyst: Deposit repricing relief and loan growth, or accelerated buybacks as capital ratios stay strong.
positions.invalidation: Consumer credit deterioration or a securities-portfolio rate shock would invalidate this application of the pricing-power thesis.

positions.name: Goldman Sachs
positions.thesis: Goldman Sachs expresses T3 and T1 through capital markets activity, because a world of sticky nominal growth and continued corporate investment supports advisory, underwriting and asset-management fees even when multiples de-rate, and at 906.22 versus a 1146.46 high after -12.0% over three months the market has already reduced its expectations; I assume the deal and IPO cycle reopens within two years, which is an assumption rather than a verified pipeline, and 2.5% reflects the higher earnings volatility of a market-sensitive bank.
positions.catalyst: A reopening of M&A, IPO and leveraged-finance issuance, or continued asset-management inflows.
positions.invalidation: A prolonged freeze in deal activity combined with trading revenue weakness would invalidate this application.

positions.name: UnitedHealth Group
positions.thesis: UnitedHealth is a managed-care and health-services company expressing T3, because in a world of sticky medical costs and aging demographics the payer can reprice annually and its integrated services earn recurring cash flow, and at 397.62 versus a 433.68 high it is below its peak with a flat three-month return despite +26.9% over twelve months; I assume medical cost ratios normalize rather than deteriorate structurally, which is an assumption about claims trends I cannot verify, and 4% reflects defensive cash flows balanced against regulatory and pricing risk.
positions.catalyst: Membership growth and pricing actions that restore margin, or continued expansion of health-services earnings.
positions.invalidation: Sustained medical cost inflation outrunning premiums, or regulatory price and rebate intervention, would invalidate this application.

positions.name: CVS Health
positions.thesis: CVS is an integrated payer, PBM and pharmacy chain applying T3 at a discount to its own high, at 85.25 versus 109.14 after -8.2% over three months, because a world of sticky healthcare spending rewards the company that owns both the insurance risk and the dispensing channel; the durable mechanism is recurring prescription and membership cash flow, but I cannot verify current margin or turnaround progress, so the weight is held at 3% and I assume integration economics improve rather than keep compressing.
positions.catalyst: PBM and payer margin recovery, Aetna medical cost normalization, or pharmacy volume and share gains.
positions.invalidation: Continued margin compression across the payer and PBM segments or a major contract loss would invalidate this application.

positions.name: Pfizer
positions.thesis: Pfizer applies T3 as a cash-generative pharmaceutical franchise whose pricing power and global demand persist under sticky inflation and aging populations, and at 29.23 versus a 30.35 high (+27.7% over twelve months) it remains in the lower half of its recent range despite the move; the evidence is the historical durability of branded pharma cash flows, an assumption that pipeline and patent-expiry management is adequate rather than verified, and 3% balances high recurring cash flow against pipeline binary risk.
positions.catalyst: Pipeline readouts, new product launches offsetting patent expiries, or accretive business development.
positions.invalidation: A deeper-than-expected patent cliff combined with pipeline failure would invalidate this application of the cash-flow thesis.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.thesis: NVIDIA is the leading accelerated-computing supplier expressing T1, because a world where AI capex keeps compounding supports continued demand for GPUs, networking and software even as the market de-rates hardware, and the packet shows 178.67 versus a 239.24 high with -17.8% over three months and -4.8% over twelve months, a substantial de-rating that I treat as a price fact rather than verified bad news; I assume compute demand and competitive position persist, which is the core uncertainty of the thesis, so 5% is the largest single tech weight and not a concentrated bet.
positions.catalyst: New hyperscaler and sovereign compute orders, continued data-center revenue growth, or software and networking mix expansion.
positions.invalidation: Cuts in hyperscaler capital expenditure, competitive silicon substitution, or export restrictions that materially impair revenue would invalidate this application.

positions.name: Alphabet Class A
positions.thesis: Alphabet expresses T1 and T3 as a cash-flow-generative search, advertising and cloud franchise that monetizes AI rather than merely spending on it, and at 288.15 versus a 402.12 high after -16.1% over three months it trades well below its 2026 peak despite a roughly flat twelve-month return; the mechanism I rely on is durable advertising and cloud cash flow funding AI investment internally, which is a known historical pattern but an unverifiable current earnings assumption, and 5% reflects quality at a de-rated price balanced against search-disruption and regulatory risk.
positions.catalyst: Cloud growth acceleration and evidence that AI features lift rather than cannibalize search monetization, plus continued buybacks.
positions.invalidation: A structural loss of search query share to AI assistants or an adverse regulatory remedy would invalidate this application.

positions.name: Microsoft
positions.thesis: Microsoft expresses T1 and T3 as a recurring-revenue software and cloud platform whose contracted subscriptions and enterprise pricing power provide short-duration, inflation-pass-through cash flow while it invests in AI infrastructure, and at 545.18 versus a 555.80 high (+10.6% over twelve months) it is near rather than at a discount to its high, so I size it at 4% rather than 5% to avoid overpaying for the same thesis; I assume cloud and enterprise IT budgets remain resilient, which I cannot verify.
positions.catalyst: Azure growth acceleration, AI copilot monetization, or sustained double-digit operating income growth.
positions.invalidation: A corporate IT spending recession or a failure to monetize AI infrastructure spending would invalidate this application.

positions.name: Amazon
positions.thesis: Amazon applies T1 through AWS and advertising and T2 through the logistics and energy demand of e-commerce, because a world of growing data workloads and steady consumer volumes supports both cloud margin expansion and retail efficiency, and at 266.93 versus a 284.02 high with -2.0% over three months and +9.8% over twelve months the price is close to its high rather than deeply discounted, so the 4% weight is a quality holding sized to avoid chasing; I assume AWS and ads keep compounding, an unverified current assumption.
positions.catalyst: AWS backlog conversion, advertising margin expansion, or retail regionalization lowering cost to serve.
positions.invalidation: A cloud slowdown or a consumer recession that compresses retail margins would invalidate this application.

positions.name: Visa
positions.thesis: Visa is a payment network expressing T3 and T1, because in a world of sticky nominal spending growth and continued digital-commerce expansion, transaction volumes and cross-border fees grow without the company carrying credit risk, and at 422.16 versus a 436.57 high (+26.3% over twelve months) it is priced as a quality compounder rather than a bargain; I assume nominal consumer spending and electronic share keep rising, and 3.5% recognizes that such durable quality is rarely cheap.
positions.catalyst: Continued electronic-payment share gains, cross-border travel recovery, or new network and value-added services revenue.
positions.invalidation: A consumer spending contraction, regulatory fee caps, or disruptive real-time payment rails would invalidate this application.

positions.name: PepsiCo
positions.thesis: PepsiCo applies T3 as a branded staples and snack company with pricing power and global distribution, because a world of sticky input costs and cautious consumers favors the brands that can hold price and regain volume, and at 141.88 versus a 165.45 high with only +4.3% over twelve months it is priced below its recent peak unlike many defensive peers; I assume volume recovery after pricing actions, which I cannot verify, and 3% is defensive ballast rather than an offensive bet.
positions.catalyst: Volume and share recovery in snacks and beverages, or input-cost relief restoring margin.
positions.invalidation: Sustained private-label share gains and consumer downtrading that force price rollbacks would invalidate this application.

positions.name: Walmart
positions.thesis: Walmart applies T3 as a scale retailer whose low-price positioning gains share in a value-seeking consumer environment and whose advertising and membership businesses add high-margin recurring revenue, and at 125.66 versus a 133.88 high (+24.6% over twelve months) it is near its high, so 3% is a defensive consumer holding sized modestly; I assume continued share gains and margin mix improvement, which are assumptions rather than verified results.
positions.catalyst: Advertising and membership revenue growth, continued grocery share gains, or operating margin expansion.
positions.invalidation: Consumer strength that shifts spending to discretionary rivals, or margin dilution from aggressive pricing, would invalidate this application.

positions.name: Altria Group
positions.thesis: Altria applies T3 as a tobacco franchise with extraordinary pricing power and high free cash flow conversion in a sticky-inflation world where nominal pricing can be raised ahead of costs, and at 75.81 versus a 78.03 high (+41.3% over twelve months) the market has already rewarded that defensiveness; the mechanism is habitual demand and pricing, which is a well-established historical pattern, and 2.5% keeps the regulatory and secular-decline risk small while still contributing income-like cash flow.
positions.catalyst: Continued pricing and dividend growth, or successful scaling of smokeless and oral nicotine products.
positions.invalidation: Accelerated excise or regulatory action, or a faster-than-expected secular volume decline, would invalidate this application.

positions.name: SPDR Gold Shares
positions.thesis: GLD expresses T4 as a hedge against fiscal dominance and currency debasement in a world of large structural deficits and sticky inflation, and at 379.53 versus a 495.90 high with -5.3% over three months and only +3.7% over twelve months the gold sleeve is well below its recent peak rather than chasing a blow-off; the mechanism is scarcity and central-bank and private demand, which I cannot verify in current data, and 4% is sized so that even a large gold drawdown cannot break the portfolio.
positions.catalyst: Renewed central-bank and private hedging demand, or a real-yield decline driven by fiscal or monetary easing.
positions.invalidation: A sustained rise in real yields with no fiscal stress, or a loss of official-sector demand, would invalidate this application of the hedge thesis.

positions.name: Bitcoin (spot)
positions.thesis: Bitcoin expresses T4 as a scarce, non-sovereign digital asset that serves as a partial debasement hedge in a world of rising public debt and fiscal dominance, and at 74314.76 versus a 86602.91 high with +8.8% over twelve months and -5.3% over three months it is well below its high, so I assume continued adoption of the network as a store of value and monetary-property asset, which is an adoption assumption rather than a verified fact; the 2.5% weight is deliberate because crypto can fall 50% or more and I accept that loss as an acceptable cost of the hedge.
positions.catalyst: Continued institutional and sovereign adoption, or a liquidity and fiscal environment that favors scarce assets.
positions.invalidation: A regulatory ban or severe restriction in major jurisdictions, or a durable loss of the store-of-value narrative to competing assets, would invalidate this application.

positions.name: Ethereum (spot)
positions.thesis: Ethereum expresses T4 and a small part of T1 as a smart-contract platform whose token is both a scarce asset and a claim on on-chain financial and computational activity, and at 2097.20 versus a 2776.47 high with -15.6% over three months it is well off its high, so I assume network usage and settlement demand grow over two years, an assumption I cannot verify; the 1% weight is intentionally the smallest in the book given the volatility and technological uncertainty of the exposure.
positions.catalyst: Growth in on-chain settlement and stablecoin or tokenized-asset activity on the network.
positions.invalidation: A technical failure, sustained loss of developer and user share to competing chains, or adverse regulation would invalidate this application.

pick.knowledgeLimitations: The snapshot gives only prices, 3- and 12-month returns and 52-week highs and lows through 2026-11-09, so I cannot verify any current valuation multiple, earnings figure, balance sheet item, macro data point, interest rate level, or news event, and I have deliberately not invented any. My training knowledge predates the snapshot date, so I cannot explain why particular names moved sharply — for example the large three-month declines in AMAT.US, CAT.US, NVDA.US, ORCL.US, CHTR.US and SE.US, or the roughly tenfold 12-month move in MRNA.US — and I treat those moves purely as price facts, not as evidence about fundamentals. I assume, without verification, that structural drivers I describe (insurance float, energy cash flows, copper demand from grids and data centers, payment volume growth, hyperscaler compute budgets) persist approximately as they have historically, and that the crypto 52-week ranges may omit weekend extremes as the packet notes.

strategies.riskRationale: This book is built for a 24-month hold with medium risk: roughly 90% of capital is spread across nine distinct economic exposures (energy, copper and machinery, defense, banks and capital markets, managed care and pharma, staples, mega-cap AI value chains, payments, conglomerate, gold and a small crypto sleeve) with no single holding above 8%, so the outcome does not depend on one company or one speculative story. I accept meaningful swings — including the possibility that the already-sharply-de-rated AI and semiconductor names fall further — in exchange for the upside of owning cash-generative franchises in energy, financials and healthcare, and I estimate a maximum peak-to-trough drawdown of about 22% during the 24 months, which is consistent with a globally diversified equity-and-real-assets mix under a medium objective rather than a low-risk preservation mandate. CashWeight of 10% is deliberate dry powder in a fragile, valuation-sensitive regime (SPY is 752.69 versus a 779.09 high, many former leaders are 30-50% below their highs, and I cannot verify the causes), and because the portfolio is never rebalanced, cash also serves as a permanent ballast that cannot be eroded by a forced sale or a margin call.

pick.risks: The main risks are concentration and correlation: the AI-capex, software and crypto sleeves all trade as high-beta risk-on exposures, so a genuine capex recession or a liquidity shock would likely hit all of them simultaneously and a 45-55% peak-to-trough decline is plausible; the semi and equipment complex is historically cyclical and could stay depressed longer than two years, crypto can lose 60-80% in a bear leg regardless of adoption trends, and the energy and copper sleeve underperforms if deflation or a recession arrives, so there is no true defensive ballast in this high-risk book.

theses.title: Underinvestment keeps real-asset cash flows elevated as power demand rises
theses.worldView: Structural underinvestment in hydrocarbons and copper supply meets rising electricity demand from data centers and electrification, so integrated energy and copper producers generate durable free cash flow and return it to holders through 2028 even if growth slows; the thesis is falsified by a sustained collapse in real energy and copper prices driven by demand destruction or a supply glut.
theses.portfolioExpression: A smaller 10% sleeve in diversified energy equity and copper exposure (XLE.US, FCX.US) applies the view that real-asset producers hedge a world where AI capex succeeds and power demand rises, and partially offsets a software-and-chips book if inflation re-accelerates.

positions.invalidation: Rising real yields, a stronger dollar, or reduced safe-haven demand could leave a non-yielding asset lagging, with no business cash flows to anchor its value.

pick.knowledgeLimitations: The snapshot supplies adjusted closes, 3- and 12-month returns, and 52-week ranges, but not current valuation multiples, earnings, cash flows, bond yields, duration, portfolio constituents, or macroeconomic data. I therefore cannot establish intrinsic value or verify 2026 business developments; company and fund descriptions reflect general knowledge, while catalysts and world theses are uncertain assumptions. A prior price decline or high is not proof of fair value.

strategies.riskRationale: The portfolio holds 60% equities for two-year upside, balanced by 25% bonds, 5% gold, and 10% cash. I estimate a 22% maximum peak-to-trough drawdown: diversification can soften a sell-off, but correlations may rise during a recession or inflation shock; the largest individual equity positions are a diversified ETF at 28% and GOOGL.US at 7%.

pick.risks: TSM.US and AMAT.US are exposed to the same semiconductor capital cycle. NOW.US and INTU.US share long-duration software and AI-replacement risks, while GOOGL.US may also fall sharply in a technology selloff. MELI.US adds currency, political, and credit exposures; NKE.US adds brand, competition, and consumer risks. The cash cushion is small, no position is rebalanced, and losses may exceed 50%.

theses.title: AI demand sustains the compute buildout
theses.worldView: Over the next 24 months, enterprise and data-center use of AI expands enough to sustain demand for leading-edge chips and manufacturing tools, although spending and winners remain cyclical. Sustained multiquarter cuts to leading-edge investment and shrinking workloads would falsify this thesis.
theses.portfolioExpression: A combined 24% in TSM.US and AMAT.US buys foundry and equipment exposure after large price reversals, with AMAT.US smaller because both depend on chipmaker capital spending.

theses.title: AI does not erase incumbent platforms
theses.worldView: AI diffusion does not make search, digital distribution, and complex enterprise workflows economically obsolete; incumbents retain enough user and enterprise demand to monetize their installed bases. Persistent usage or renewal losses, or materially weaker monetization as AI substitutes for these services, would falsify this thesis.
theses.portfolioExpression: Use GOOGL.US, NOW.US, and INTU.US as possible beneficiaries or survivors. The deep NOW.US and INTU.US drawdowns and GOOGL.US's recent retracement are a contrarian screen, not proof that their multiples or intrinsic values are cheap.

theses.title: Latin American commerce keeps moving online
theses.worldView: Through November 2028, Latin American online commerce and electronic payments continue gaining transaction share despite currency and political volatility. Sustained stagnation in adoption, or credit and regulatory shocks that overwhelm usage growth, would falsify this thesis.
theses.portfolioExpression: A 14% position in MELI.US expresses this structural shift through a marketplace and payments ecosystem, capped for regional macroeconomic, currency, credit, and valuation risk.

theses.title: Athletic apparel remains a durable category
theses.worldView: Global demand for athletic footwear and apparel remains durable, and consumers continue to reward differentiated brands despite cyclical purchasing. Persistent brand share losses and discounting would falsify this thesis.
theses.portfolioExpression: A 12% position in NKE.US is a contrarian exposure to a global consumer category after a substantial price decline, not a claim that all consumer stocks are cheap.

theses.title: A market correction remains plausible
theses.worldView: Within the next 24 months, SPY.US records at least one closing drawdown of 10% or more from a prior closing peak, with sharp rotations rather than an uninterrupted advance. The absence of such a decline would falsify this thesis.
theses.portfolioExpression: Eight percent remains in zero-return cash as a small static buffer against that risk. It is not assumed to be reinvested and will dilute returns if equities rise.

pick.thesis: This is a concentrated, contrarian bet that AI-related demand and embedded digital platforms endure while selected commerce and brand drawdowns recover. Position caps and 8% zero-yield cash reflect the possibility that the price declines signal lasting impairment rather than value.

forecasts.reason: An approximately 26% total return is plausible if AI investment remains funded, incumbent search and workflow products adapt rather than lose their economics, and portions of the software, Latin American commerce, and apparel drawdowns recover. This requires no severe recession or Taiwan disruption and could fail badly if the selloffs reflect lasting impairment.

positions.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A
positions.thesis: Alphabet owns search, YouTube, Android, and a cloud business; its user and advertiser distribution is a durable mechanism under the incumbent-platform thesis, while AI demand could also benefit its services. The 2026-11-09 close of $288.15 was down 16.1% over three months and 28.3% from the $402.12 52-week high, though only 5.5% above the $273.16 low. That retracement creates a contrarian entry if search monetization survives, but the packet supplies no valuation multiple. The 18% weight is the largest because its platform is less tied to a single chip-capex cycle, though AI and regulatory risks still warrant a cap.
positions.catalyst: AI products support useful search, cloud, and advertising services without materially eroding the economics of intent-based advertising, or confidence in the existing platform normalizes.
positions.invalidation: The thesis fails if AI answer services divert queries and advertising faster than Alphabet can monetize them, antitrust remedies materially impair its distribution, or competition weakens the returns on its investment.

positions.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company
positions.thesis: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company operates contract semiconductor foundries, turning chip designs into manufactured chips; the AI-buildout thesis treats advanced manufacturing capacity as strategically important. Its supplied close of $388.62 was about 20% below the $485.80 52-week high after a 7.7% three-month decline, though it remained up 35.8% over twelve months. Scale, process know-how, and customer qualification are durable mechanisms, but price history does not establish an attractive valuation multiple. The 14% weight buys secular-demand exposure while limiting dependence on one capital-intensive, Taiwan-centered supplier.
positions.catalyst: Continued demand for advanced chips supports foundry utilization and investment, restoring confidence that the recent pullback was cyclical rather than structural.
positions.invalidation: A foundry downcycle, lost technology or customer competitiveness, a serious Taiwan disruption, or sustained cuts to leading-edge investment would break the thesis.

positions.name: Applied Materials
positions.thesis: Applied Materials sells equipment and services used in semiconductor manufacturing. Its $370.55 close was 48.7% below the $722.23 52-week high after a 29.4% three-month fall, although it was still up 59.6% over twelve months. The technical complexity and long qualification cycles of chipmaking equipment are durable mechanisms; the sharp reversal is a candidate expectation reset, not verified evidence of undervaluation. The 10% weight is smaller than TSM.US because equipment spending is cyclical and the two positions overlap.
positions.catalyst: Orders and service activity stabilize as chipmakers continue investing in manufacturing capacity, showing that the recent decline was not the start of a prolonged spending contraction.
positions.invalidation: A sustained semiconductor-capex contraction, restrictions that materially reduce addressable demand, or lost equipment competitiveness would falsify the application of the AI-buildout thesis.

positions.name: ServiceNow
positions.thesis: ServiceNow sells enterprise workflow and IT-service management software; the incumbent-platform thesis expects complex organizations to keep relying on embedded workflows and to adopt AI within them rather than replace them wholesale. Its $102.76 close was 40.8% below the $173.50 52-week high, with returns of -40.2% over twelve months and -19.4% over three months. That repricing makes a recovery plausible if the workflows remain important, but the packet provides no financials or multiples to prove intrinsic value is higher. The 12% weight reflects its potential durability while capping its software and AI-execution risk.
positions.catalyst: Enterprise software budgets stabilize, or paid AI workflow use demonstrates that customers are extending rather than abandoning the platform.
positions.invalidation: The thesis fails if generative agents displace core workflows, customers cut subscriptions, or pricing and renewals weaken persistently.

positions.name: Intuit
positions.thesis: Intuit provides tax-preparation and small-business accounting software; trusted tax and accounting workflows and customer records could remain valuable as AI diffuses. Its $338.23 close was 49.3% below the $667.14 52-week high, and the snapshot shows a 47.5% twelve-month decline. That is a substantial expectations reset, not evidence by itself that the shares are undervalued. The 12% weight is a capped contrarian bet because AI automation could challenge these products and the position overlaps with NOW.US and GOOGL.US.
positions.catalyst: A future tax cycle and product improvements demonstrate continued customer use and AI-assisted monetization rather than substitution.
positions.invalidation: The thesis fails if free or bundled AI and competing services commoditize tax preparation or bookkeeping, or if a sustained small-business slowdown weakens customer demand.

positions.name: MercadoLibre
positions.thesis: MercadoLibre operates an online marketplace and payments and financial-services ecosystem in Latin America; continued migration of commerce and payments online could reinforce its network effects despite uneven regional growth. Its 2026-11-09 close of $1,532.68 was just 1.5% above the $1,510 52-week low and 33.2% below the $2,295 high, with returns of -21.0% over three months and -28.0% over twelve months. The decline is an entry only if the network economics persist, not proof of undervaluation. The 14% stake adds regional growth exposure but is capped for currency, political, credit, and valuation risk.
positions.catalyst: Online commerce and merchant-payment activity remain resilient through a less favorable regional backdrop, supporting a recovery in confidence in the ecosystem's network economics.
positions.invalidation: Currency or political shocks, credit losses, competition, or prolonged consumer weakness could erode those economics; a price near the 52-week low may signal deterioration rather than excessive pessimism.

positions.name: Nike
positions.thesis: Nike sells branded athletic footwear and apparel globally; the sportswear-demand thesis is that consumers will continue to value differentiated athletic brands and global distribution. At $39.88, it was 39.6% below the $66.04 52-week high and 17.7% above the $33.87 low, with a 33.4% twelve-month decline. This makes it a contrarian value candidate only if brand relevance and demand endure; the packet supplies no inventory, sales, or valuation evidence to establish that. The 12% weight limits the risk of a failed brand recovery.
positions.catalyst: Improved product demand and a return to healthier full-price sales would support a recovery in confidence in the brand and category.
positions.invalidation: The thesis fails if consumer preferences shift away, competitors take sustained share, discounting remains entrenched, or discretionary demand weakens for a prolonged period.
